criteria.demonstration: The explicit product state separates accepted framed bytes, confirmed durable prefix/epoch, write diagnostic and two uncertainty kinds. IO with the final accepted bytes remains IO. Known flush IO may advance confirmed durability; unknown acknowledgement retains prior authority. No write, cancellation or local memory release is treated as rollback or physical durability.

criteria.demonstration: The copied staging adapter imports actual PR-T19-04 io.stream sf_start/pump/cancel and actual er_transfer, preserving the original framing and generation contracts. A synchronous bridge keeps count and diagnostic separate, bounds relative progress and retains copied ownership through cancellation or uncertainty. Admission/refusal and quiescent release have explicit unchanged-output or retained-owner rules.

criteria.demonstration: Changed-condition support executes copied-input mutation, cancellation after a two-byte prefix, explicit abandonment, stale generations, finite epochs and trusted lost-acknowledgement reconciliation. An actual nonblocking pipe reaches EAGAIN; an owned file has two actual fsync successes separated from injected pre-call refusal and post-success lost reply. The controller authority is explicit, not inferred from readable bytes. All13cost dimensions, seven workload samples, current producer imports and clean/incremental builds are retained; no asynchronous syscall cancellation or power-loss proof is claimed.

limits: Live stable controls, disjoint storage and synchronous nonreentrant callbacks are explicit preconditions.
Accepted framed bytes are not application effects or durable commits.
Trusted reconciliation requires actual external authority; numeric checks do not prove it.
Known real fsync success and injected reply loss are not reboot, directory or physical power-loss evidence.
No arbitrary concurrent callback cancellation, independent-human assessment or learner mastery; published C17/C23 inaccessible.
